basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 1-5.' and it opens 'VERS. 1-5.--Deinde sequitur qualiter Abraham, mortua Saraa, aliam, videlicet Cethuram,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 1-5.--Deinde sequitur qualiter Abraham, mortua Saraa, aliam, videlicet Cethuram, duxerit uxorem. Cur Abraham post promissum sibi et natum Isaac, in quo ei multiplicatio prolis et benedictio | gentium promissa est a Deo, aliam voluit ducere uxorem? Non propter incontinentiam, cum etiam esset grandaevus; sed sicut Agar et Ismael significant carnales Veteris Testamenti, sic et Cethura et filii ejus significant haereticos, qui se existimant pertinere ad Novum Testamentum. Sed utraeque concubinae dicuntur. Sic enim dicitur:
